sentences.span: The 10-year yield broke 4.40% on Friday for the first time since May.
We think the move is a bear-steepener: the front end is anchored by a Fed on hold, so the long end is doing the work as term premium rebuilds.
sentences.why: Document is JPMorgan's own note ('J.P. Morgan Rates Strategy'), so 'We think' is JPMorgan's view; bear-steepener framing and front-end/Fed-on-hold rationale match verbatim.

sentences.span: We recommend paying 5s30s at 62bp with a stop at 48bp. Citi's rates desk, by contrast, sees the break as a positioning flush and expects 4.40% to hold on a closing basis.
sentences.why: The paying 5s30s at 62bp/48bp-stop trade is JPMorgan's own recommendation ('We recommend'), not Citi's. Citi's actual view in the source is the opposite: it reads the break as a positioning flush and expects 4.40% to hold. The sentence swaps the trade call's attribution to the bank that source text explicitly disagrees with it.
No source document mentions Goldman, a 4.75% year-end target, or fading foreign demand. Only JPMorgan and Citi appear in the source, and neither is quoted with a numeric year-end level.

sentences.span: A hot core PCE print on Thursday (consensus 0.3% m/m) would validate our steepener; a soft print would not by itself reverse it while the Fed stays on hold.
sentences.why: Matches the source's framing of Thursday's core PCE print (0.3% m/m consensus) as the condition that validates the steepener call.
